properties.evidence: That idea compares embedded engines on the assumption that the engine is what costs. Measured with NO engine at all — in-memory backend, no RocksDB, no tantivy — hydrate is still 8.8s at 3,140 nodes, with 95% of it inside import_graph and only 4% in JSON parsing. Whichever engine wins that comparison, it cannot move the number that matters, so the premise the comparison rests on is contradicted rather than merely unsupported.
